s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive scalp mass with ulceration and bleeding, associated with cervical lymphadenopathy and suspected distant metastases
salient_findings: Recent rapid growth, ulceration, and bleeding of the mass
key_facts: 49-year-old woman of African origin
Right-sided scalp mass present for 10 years
Mass was stable and nontender until recent excision
No histopathology was done after excision
Mass recurred, enlarged, ulcerated, and bled easily over 5 months
Patient denies headaches, convulsions, or neurologic deficits
Afebrile and hemodynamically stable on examination
No pallor, jaundice, or palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy
Two lesions on the right side of the scalp
Fungating, tender, 9 × 7 cm mass prone to bleeding
Second non-fungating, 3 × 3 cm lesion
Normal complete blood count and basic metabolic panel
Unremarkable chest radiography and abdominal/pelvic ultrasound
Head and neck CT scan showed multilobulated, hyperdense, ulcerative right frontal scalp lesion
Enlarged cervical lymph nodes at levels I and II
MRI of the spine revealed pathological compression fracture of T10 and hyperintense lesion in T8

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common cause of scalp masses with ulceration and bleeding

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common skin cancer that can cause scalp masses, although less likely to ulcerate and bleed

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive skin cancer that can cause scalp masses and has a high risk of metastasis

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but aggressive cancer that can cause scalp masses and has a high risk of bleeding

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive skin cancer that can cause scalp masses and has a high risk of metastasis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a long-standing scalp mass that became ulcerated, bled easily, and recurred after excision, along with the presence of a fungating mass and cervical lymphadenopathy, is most consistent with squamous cell carcinoma, a common skin cancer that can be aggressive and metastasize.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically less aggressive and less likely to metastasize

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Rare and typically presents with more rapid growth and neurologic symptoms

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Rare and typically presents with more extensive skin involvement and systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Malignant melanoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a pigmented lesion and more rapid progression
